conclusion: Per super-block both kernels perform exactly the same six floating-point operations on the same operands in the same order: two fp16->fp32 conversions, two fmul, one fused fmsub, one fused fmadd, with the running sum threaded through the fused ops. Operand order of the commutative fmul differs syntactically (x.d*y.d vs y.d*x.d) but not in result. Spilling of dmin/sumf to the stack in V0 vs register residency in V1 does not alter values (fp32 store/load is exact). The int32->fp32 conversion of sumi uses the same rounding mode in both (scvtf, RN) and is exact for the reachable |sumi| range.
note_on_exactness: |sumi| bound from the manuscript is 3.1e7 (< 2^25); fp32 has 24 significand bits, so conversion may round for |sumi| in [2^24, 2^25). Both kernels apply the identical scvtf to the identical int32, so any such rounding is identical — exactness is not required for FT2, identity is.
status_of_500_500_agreement: The system-level 500/500 identical outputs are E2 corroboration of this reading, not its basis.

sumf_accumulator_V0.reading: fmsub s0 = s4 - s0*s3 = sumf - f(sumi_mins)*dmin ; fmadd s0 = s1*s17 + s0 = f(sumi)*d + (...) ; stored back to [sp,#0x78]
